claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you are looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my one child, Alex. They're 8 years old and I'd like to know if I can get Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask a few more questions.

Are you responsible for Alex? This typically means that Alex lives with you, or you contribute towards the cost of looking after them (at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me. I'm their parent and they live at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Could you tell me, is Alex in full-time education or training? And if so, are they enrolled in a course that is either:
- Non-advanced education (such as GCSEs, A-levels, or equivalent), or
- An approved training course?

(Since Alex is 8 years old, I expect they are in primary school, but I just want to confirm their education status.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in primary school - just regular school for their age. Nothing special or advanced, just the normal education that 8-year-olds do.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions:

Do you (the person who would be claiming Child Benefit) live in the United Kingdom?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, I need to ask a few follow-up questions to understand your situation better.

Are you working abroad in any of the following capacities:
- As a Crown servant (for example, working for the UK government, diplomatic or consular staff)
- As a member of the UK armed forces
- Working for a UK-based employer paying National Insurance contributions in the UK

Or are you living abroad for other reasons?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply to me. I'm just living abroad for other reasons - not working for the UK government or armed forces or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information I've gathered and the eligibility rules, I now have enough details to make a determination about your Child Benefit eligibility for Alex.

The key eligibility requirement is that the person claiming Child Benefit must normally **live in the UK**. While there are some exceptions for people living abroad (such as Crown servants, armed forces members, or those working for UK employers and paying UK National Insurance), you've confirmed that none of these exceptions apply to your situation.

Unfortunately, since you are living abroad and are not in any of the exempt categories, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Summary:**

| Child | Eligible? | Reason |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Alex | No | The claimant does not live in the UK |

**Explanation:**

Although Alex meets several of the criteria (being under 16, in full-time education, and living with you as their parent), one of the fundamental requirements for Child Benefit is that the person claiming must **live in the UK**.

Since you are living abroad and do not fall into any of the exempt categories (such as being a Crown servant, member of the UK armed forces, or working for a UK employer while paying UK National Insurance), you unfortunately cannot claim Child Benefit at this time.

If your circumstances change and you return to live in the UK, you would likely become eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you have any other questions or your situation changes, please don't hesitate to reach out.
